name: VCSS
comment: Vixen's stylesheet language: CSS, plus the four at-rules the utility generator reads. The Vixen-specific patterns come first and `source.css` is included last, so anything not claimed here is coloured exactly as CSS — which is the point, since VCSS *is* CSS everywhere it does not say otherwise.

theme.comment: @theme is where a project's design tokens live, and a token is a custom property — so declaring `--color-brand` both makes `var(--color-brand)` available and tells the generator that `bg-brand`, `text-brand` and `border-brand` exist. That is why the names inside are scoped as definitions rather than as ordinary properties.
theme.name: meta.at-rule.theme.vcss

patterns.comment: `--color-*: initial` is how a project removes a whole namespace the engine ships, and `--breakpoint-*: initial` how it clears the five page-sized defaults. The star is part of the name.

apply.comment: @apply expands utility class names inside a rule. The build expands it on the way through, so the names after it are the same vocabulary a class attribute holds.

layer.comment: Both forms: the statement that fixes the order — `@layer base, components, utilities;` — and the block. ⚠ The statement is the load-bearing one: layer order belongs to whoever names a layer first, so a sheet concatenated ahead of the generated utilities has to say all three or the ladder comes out wrong.

tag-selector.comment: ⚠ **The one place VCSS looks wrong in a CSS editor.** Vixen's element names are the control library's — `menu-bar`, `dock-panel`, `progress-bar`, and whatever a component's `@tag` says — so almost every type selector here is a hyphenated name that CSS's own grammar does not know and colours as an unknown tag. Matched at the head of a rule so that it reads as the element name it is.
tag-selector.name: entity.name.tag.vcss

comment.comment: ⚠ CSS comments do not nest and have no escape: the first star-slash closes one. Worth knowing here because a token file's header is usually a long prose block, and a glob pattern written literally inside it ends the comment on its own second line and feeds the rest to the parser as CSS. That has happened.
comment.name: comment.block.vcss
